correct: For diabetes, Point-of-care A1C testing for diabetes screening and diagnosis should be restricted to U.S. Food and Drug Administration–approved devices at laboratories proficient in performing testing of moderate complexity or higher by trained personnel.
wrong: For diabetes, Point-of-care A1C testing for diabetes screening and diagnosis should be restricted to U.S. Food and Drug Administration–approved devices at laboratories proficient in performing testing of low complexity or higher by trained personnel.

correct: For diabetes, Statin therapy may increase the risk of type 2 diabetes in people at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In such individuals, glucose status should be monitored regularly and diabetes prevention approaches reinforced. It is not recommended that statins be discontinued
wrong: For diabetes, Statin therapy may increase the risk of type 2 diabetes in people at high risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In such individuals, glucose status should be monitored regularly and diabetes prevention approaches reinforced. It is not recommended that statins be continued.

correct: For diabetes, In people with a history of stroke and evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes, pioglitazone may be considered to lower the risk of stroke or myocardial infarction.
wrong: For diabetes, In people with a history of stroke and evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes, pioglitazone is not recommended for lowering the risk of stroke or myocardial infarction.

correct: For diabetes, Lower doses of pioglitazone may mitigate the risk of adverse effects in people with a history of stroke and evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes.
wrong: For diabetes, Lower doses of pioglitazone may not sufficiently mitigate the risk of adverse effects in people with a history of stroke and evidence of insulin resistance and prediabetes.

correct: For diabetes, More intensive preventive approaches should be considered in individuals who are at particularly high risk of progression to diabetes, including individuals with BMI ≥35 kg/m2, those at higher glucose levels (e.g., fasting plasma glucose 110–125 mg/dL, 2-h postchallenge glucose 173–199 mg/dL, A1C ≥6.0%), and individuals with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus.
wrong: For diabetes, More intensive preventive approaches should be considered in individuals who are at particularly high risk of progression to diabetes, including individuals with BMI ≥35 kg/m2, those at higher glucose levels (e.g., fasting plasma glucose 100–110 mg/dL, 2-h postchallenge glucose 140–160 mg/dL, A1C ≥5.5%), and individuals with a history of gestational diabetes mellitus.

correct: For diabetes, Patients with diabetes cau use PCV15 and PCV20 for diabetes patients who face higher risks of severe pneumococcal disease.
wrong: For diabetes, Patients with diabetes are not recommended to use PCV15 and PCV20 for diabetes patients. These vaccines may decrease insulin sensitivity in some patients and have been associated with adverse immunological responses in this population.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with diabetes should receive one dose of PCV15 or PCV20. If PCV15 is administered, it should be followed by PPSV23 after ≥1 year interval.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with diabetes should receive one dose of PCV15 or PCV20. If PCV15 is administered, it should be followed by PPSV23 after ≥6 months interval.

correct: For diabetes, For immunocompromised patients with diabetes, those with cochlear implants, or cerebrospinal fluid leaks, a minimum interval of 8 weeks (rather than 1 year) can be considered between PCV15 and PPSV23 administration.
wrong: For diabetes, For immunocompromised patients with diabetes, those with cochlear implants, or cerebrospinal fluid leaks, a minimum interval of 4 weeks (rather than 1 year) can be considered between PCV15 and PPSV23 administration.

correct: For diabetes, Those who received only PPSV23 may now receive PCV15 or PCV20 ≥1 year after their last PPSV23 dose.
wrong: For diabetes, Those who received only PPSV23 may now receive PCV15 or PCV20 ≥6 months after their last PPSV23 dose.

correct: For diabetes, Novavax COVID-19 vaccine is available as a protein-based alternative for patients with diabetes who may have concerns about mRNA technology.
wrong: For diabetes, Novavax COVID-19 vaccine is not recommended as a protein-based alternative for patients with diabetes who may have concerns about mRNA technology, as its benefits in this population remain unclear.

correct: For diabetes, For adults with diabetes, Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) COVID-19 vaccine is now limited due to safety considerations.
wrong: For diabetes, For adults with diabetes, the Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) COVID-19 vaccine may be considered as a safe option.

correct: For diabetes, Patients with diabetes continue to be cautioned against taking the live attenuated influenza vaccine (nasal spray) and should instead receive the inactive or recombinant influenza vaccination.
wrong: For diabetes, Patients with diabetes may consider receiving the live attenuated influenza vaccine (nasal spray).

correct: For diabetes, For individuals with diabetes ≥65 years of age, there may be additional benefit from the high-dose quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine.
wrong: For diabetes, For individuals with diabetes ≥65 years of age, the standard-dose inactivated influenza vaccine is sufficient and provides comparable protection to the high-dose quadrivalent inactivated influenza vaccine.

correct: For diabetes, Hepatitis B vaccine continues to be recommended for all adults with diabetes aged <60 years.
wrong: For diabetes, Hepatitis B vaccine continues to be recommended for all adults with diabetes aged <70 years.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, especially those with obesity or cardiometabolic risk factors, should be screened for significant nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (moderate fibrosis to cirrhosis) using the fibrosis-4 index, even with normal liver enzymes.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, especially those with obesity or cardiometabolic risk factors, may consider screening for significant nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (moderate fibrosis to cirrhosis) using the fibrosis-4 index, only when liver enzymes are elevated.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with diabetes or prediabetes with persistently elevated plasma aminotransferase levels for >6 months and low fibrosis-4 index should be evaluated for other causes of liver disease.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with diabetes or prediabetes with persistently elevated plasma aminotransferase levels for >3 months and low fibrosis-4 index may consider evaluation for other causes of liver disease.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with an indeterminate or high fibrosis-4 index should have additional risk stratification by liver stiffness measurement with transient elastography, or the blood biomarker enhanced liver fibrosis.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with an indeterminate or high fibrosis-4 index should be monitored with regular follow-up FIB-4 testing, without additional specialized testing unless clinical symptoms of liver disease develop or liver enzymes become abnormal.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with indeterminate results or at high risk for significant liver fibrosis (i.e., by fibrosis-4 index, liver stiffness measurement, or enhanced liver fibrosis) should be referred to a gastroenterologist or hepatologist for further workup. Multidisciplinary care is recommended for long-term management.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with indeterminate results or at high risk for significant liver fibrosis (i.e., by fibrosis-4 index, liver stiffness measurement, or enhanced liver fibrosis) may consider consultation with a gastroenterologist or hepatologist for further evaluation. Management by Multidisciplinary care providers is recommended for short-term management.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes particularly with overweight or obesity with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease should be recommended lifestyle changes that promote weight loss, ideally within a structured nutrition plan and physical activity program for cardiometabolic benefits and histological improvement.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes particularly with overweight or obesity with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease may consider optional lifestyle adjustments that permit gradual weight loss, through general dietary advice and occasional physical activity for potential liver enzyme normalization.

correct: For diabetes, For adults with type 2 diabetes particularly with overweight or obesity with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, consider using a glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist with demonstrated benefits in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis as an adjunctive therapy to lifestyle interventions for weight loss.
wrong: For diabetes, For adults with type 2 diabetes, particularly those with overweight or obesity and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, lifestyle interventions for weight loss are the primary recommended therapy; pharmacological agents have not shown sufficient benefits in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.

correct: For diabetes, Pioglitazone or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists are the preferred agents for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with biopsy-proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, or those at high risk for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease with clinically significant liver fibrosis using noninvasive tests.
wrong: For diabetes, Metformin or sitagliptin are the preferred agents for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with biopsy-proven nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, or those at high risk for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease with clinically significant liver fibrosis using noninvasive tests.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, use of glucose-lowering therapies other than pioglitazone or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists may be continued as clinically indicated, but these therapies lack evidence of benefit in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, use of glucose-lowering therapies other than pioglitazone or glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists should be avoided.

correct: For diabetes, Insulin therapy is the preferred agent for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with decompensated cirrhosis.
wrong: For diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors are the preferred agent for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with decompensated cirrhosis.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease are at increased cardiovascular risk; therefore, comprehensive management of cardiovascular risk factors is recommended.
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease may have cardiovascular risk; therefore, selective management of cardiovascular risk factors is recommended.

correct: For diabetes, Statin therapy is safe in adults with type 2 diabetes and compensated cirrhosis from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and should be initiated or continued for cardiovascular risk reduction as clinically indicated.
wrong: For diabetes, Statin therapy is not particularly safe in adults with type 2 diabetes and compensated cirrhosis from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and should be avoided for cardiovascular risk reduction when clinically possible.

correct: For diabetes, Statin therapy should be used with caution and close monitoring in people with decompensated cirrhosis, given limited safety and efficacy data.
wrong: For diabetes, Statins were contraindicated in patients with active liver disease or decompensated cirrhosis due to concerns about hepatotoxicity and lack of efficacy data.

correct: For diabetes, Consider metabolic surgery in appropriate candidates as an option to treat nonalcoholic steatohepatitis in adults with type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis and improve cardiovascular outcomes.
wrong: For diabetes, Metabolic surgery is generally not considered a primary intervention for nonalcoholic steatohepatitis in adults with type 2 diabetes. Focus management on lifestyle modifications, glycemic control, and pharmacological therapies targeting insulin resistance and hepatic inflammation.

correct: For diabetes, Metabolic surgery should be used with caution in adults with type 2 diabetes with compensated cirrhosis from nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and is not recommended in decompensated cirrhosis.
wrong: For diabetes, Metabolic surgery can be cautiously performed in adults with type 2 diabetes and compensated cirrhosis due to nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, as well as in those with decompensated cirrhosis.

correct: For diabetes, In people with preclinical type 1 diabetes, monitor for disease progression using A1C approximately every 6 months and 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (i.e., fasting and 2-h plasma glucose) annually; modify frequency of monitoring based on individual risk assessment based on age, number and type of autoantibodies, and glycemic metrics.
wrong: For diabetes, In people with preclinical type 1 diabetes, monitor for disease progression using A1C approximately every 9 months and 75-g oral glucose tolerance test (i.e., fasting and 2-h plasma glucose) quarterly; modify frequency of monitoring based on individual risk assessment based on age, number and type of autoantibodies, and glycemic metrics.

correct: For diabetes, Teplizumab-mzwv infusion to delay the onset of symptomatic type 1 diabetes (stage 3) should be considered in selected individuals aged ≥8 years with stage 2 type 1 diabetes.
wrong: For diabetes, Individuals aged 8 years or older with stage 2 type 1 diabetes should undergo regular monitoring for progression to symptomatic type 1 diabetes (stage 3). At this time, Teplizumab-mzwv infusion is not recommended.

correct: For diabetes, Monitor bone mineral density using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry of high-risk older adults with diabetes (aged >65 years) and younger individuals with diabetes and multiple risk factors every 2–3 years.
wrong: For diabetes, Monitor bone mineral density using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry of older adults with diabetes (aged >70 years) and individuals with diabetes and multiple risk factors every 5 years.

correct: For diabetes, Clinicians should consider the potential adverse impact on bone health when selecting pharmacological options to lower glucose levels in people with diabetes. Prioritizing medications with a proven safety profile for bones is recommended, particularly for those at elevated risk for fractures.
wrong: For diabetes, Clinicians should primarily focus on glucose-lowering efficacy and overall metabolic benefits when selecting pharmacological options for people with diabetes. While monitoring for major common side effects, there is insufficient evidence to suggest that bone health considerations should influence medication selection for patients with diabetes.

correct: For diabetes, To reduce the risk of falls and fractures, glycemic management goals should be individualized for people with diabetes at a higher risk of fracture. Prioritize use of glucose-lowering medications that are associated with low risk for hypoglycemia to avoid falls.
wrong: For diabetes, Standard glycemic management protocols are generally appropriate for all diabetes patients, including those with fracture risk. Treatment should prioritize achieving glycemic targets, with medication selection based primarily on glucose-lowering efficacy.

correct: For diabetes, Antiresorptive medications and osteoanabolic agents should be considered for people with diabetes who have low bone mineral density with a T-score ≤−2.0 or have experienced fragility fractures.
wrong: For diabetes, Antiresorptive medications and osteoanabolic agents should be considered for people with diabetes who have low bone mineral density with a T-score ≤−2.5 or have experienced fragility fractures.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have T-scores of −2.0 or lower should be considered at high fracture risk.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have T-scores of −2.5 or lower should be considered at high fracture risk.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have had the condition for more than 10 years correlate with higher fracture risk, necessitating bone health assessment.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have had the condition for more than 15 years are associated with increased fracture risk, warranting bone health assessment.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes using insulin, thiazolidinediones, or sulfonylureas should be evaluated for increased fracture risk.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes using metformin, DPP-4 inhibitors, or SGLT2 inhibitors should be evaluated for increased fracture risk.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have poor glycemic control (A1C >8%) are associated with higher fracture risk and should prompt bone health assessment.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have good glycemic control (A1C >6%) are associated with higher fracture risk and should prompt bone health assessment.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have neuropathy require evaluation for fall risk and bone health.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetic neuropathy should primarily focus on pain management and monitoring of sensory loss; fall risk assessment should be considered when patients report obvious balance problems.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have microvascular complications like retinopathy and nephropathy indicate increased fracture risk.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes who have microvascular complications like retinopathy and nephropathy are associated with average fracture risk.

correct: For diabetes, Deintensify hypoglycemia-causing medications (insulin, sulfonylureas, or meglitinides), or switch to a medication class with lower hypoglycemia risk, for individuals who are at high risk for hypoglycemia, within individualized glycemic goals.
wrong: For diabetes, Deintensify medications known to cause hypoglycemia (dipepepideyl peptididase-4 inhibitors, sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors, or thiazolidinediones), or switch to a medication class with higher risk of hypoglycemia, for individuals who are at high risk for hypoglycemia, within individualized glycemic goals.

correct: For diabetes, Monitor individuals who have undergone metabolic surgery for insufficient weight loss or weight recurrence at least every 6–12 months.
wrong: For diabetes, Monitor individuals who have undergone metabolic surgery for excessive weight loss or weight gain at least every 12–18 months.

correct: For diabetes, Aim for approximately 7 hours of sleep per night to help reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, as both shorter and longer sleep durations are associated with increased risk.
wrong: For diabetes, Aim for approximately 8 hours of sleep per night to help reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, as both shorter and longer sleep durations are associated with increased risk.

correct: For diabetes, Avoid regularly sleeping less than 6 hours or more than 9 hours per night, as both patterns may increase your risk of developing type 2 diabetes.
wrong: For diabetes, Avoid regularly sleeping more than 10 hours per night, as both patterns may increase your risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

correct: For diabetes, Consider adopting an earlier sleep schedule (going to bed earlier and waking up earlier), as evening chronotypes have up to 2.5 times higher risk of type 2 diabetes compared to morning chronotypes.
wrong: For diabetes, Maintaining a consistent sleep schedule aligned with your natural chronotype (whether you are a morning person or a night owl) is essential for adequate and regular sleep. Chronotype itself does not significantly impact the risk of type 2 diabetes, provided that sleep are adequate and regular.

correct: For diabetes, Consider the potential adverse impact on skeletal health when selecting pharmacological options to lower glucose levels in people with diabetes. Avoiding medications with a known association with higher fracture risk (e.g., thiazolidinediones and sulfonylureas) is recommended, particularly for those at elevated risk for fractures.
wrong: For diabetes, When managing hyperglycemia in diabetic patients, consider the potential adverse impact of certain glucose-lowering medications on skeletal health. Thiazolidinediones and sulfonylureas may be preferred options.

correct: For diabetes, Advise people with diabetes on their intake of calcium (1,000–1,200 mg/day) and vitamin D to ensure it meets the recommended daily allowance for those at risk for fracture, either through their diet or supplemental means.
wrong: For diabetes, Advise people with diabetes on their intake of calcium (800–1,000 mg/day) and vitamin D to ensure it meets the recommended daily allowance for those at risk for fracture, either through their diet or supplemental means.

correct: For diabetes, Antiresorptive medications and osteoanabolic agents should be recommended for older adults with diabetes who are at higher risk of fracture, including those with low bone mineral density with a T-score ≤−2.0, history of fragility fracture, or elevated Fracture Risk Assessment Tool score (≥3% for hip fracture or ≥20% for major osteoporotic fracture).
wrong: For diabetes, Antiresorptive medications and osteoanabolic agents should be recommended for older adults with diabetes who are at higher risk of fracture, including those with low bone mineral density with a T-score ≤−1.5, history of fragility fracture, or elevated Fracture Risk Assessment Tool score (≥2% for hip fracture or ≥15% for major osteoporotic fracture).

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes should be referred for a dental exam at least once per year.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes should be referred for a dental exam at least once per two years.

correct: For diabetes, In men with diabetes or prediabetes, screen for ED, particularly in those with high cardiovascular risk, retinopathy, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, peripheral or autonomic neuropathy, longer duration of diabetes, depression, and hypogonadism, and in those who are not meeting glycemic goals.
wrong: For diabetes, Screen for erectile dysfunction only in men with longstanding diabetes (>10 years) who actively report sexual dysfunction symptoms. ED screening is not routinely needed for men with prediabetes or well-controlled diabetes (HbA1c <7.0%).

correct: For diabetes, In women with diabetes or prediabetes, inquire about sexual health by screening for desire (libido), arousal, and orgasm difficulties, particularly in those who experience depression and/or anxiety and those with recurrent urinary tract infections.
wrong: For diabetes, In women with diabetes or prediabetes, inquire about sexual health by screening for desire (libido), arousal, and orgasm difficulties, particularly in those who with recurrent yeast infections.

correct: For diabetes, Screen adults with type 2 diabetes or with prediabetes, particularly those with obesity or other cardiometabolic risk factors or established cardiovascular disease, for their risk of having or developing cirrhosis related to metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) using a calculated fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), even if they have normal liver enzymes.
wrong: For diabetes, For adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes—especially those with obesity, additional cardiometabolic risk factors, or established cardiovascular disease—screen for cirrhosis related to metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) using a calculated fibrosis‑4 index (FIB‑4) when abnormal liver enzymes are present.

correct: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with a FIB-4 ≥1.3 should have additional risk stratification by liver stiffness measurement with transient elastography, or, if unavailable, the enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF) test
wrong: For diabetes, Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with a FIB-4 ≥1.1 should have additional risk stratification by liver stiffness measurement with transient elastography, or, if unavailable, the enhanced liver fibrosis (ELF) test

correct: For diabetes, Refer adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes at higher risk for significant liver fibrosis (i.e., as indicated by FIB-4, liver stiffness measurement, or ELF) to a gastroenterologist or hepatologist for further evaluation and management.
wrong: For diabetes, Refer adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes at lower risk for significant liver fibrosis (i.e., as indicated by FIB-4, liver stiffness measurement, or ELF) to a gastroenterologist or hepatologist for further evaluation and management.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes, MASLD, and overweight or obesity, consider using a glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (RA) or a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 RA for the treatment of obesity with potential benefits in MASH as an adjunctive therapy to lifestyle interventions for weight loss.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes, MASLD, and overweight or obesity, consider using a dipeptidyl peptidase‑4 (DPP‑4) inhibitor or a dual glucose‑dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and DPP‑4 inhibitor for the treatment of obesity with potential benefits in MASH as an adjunctive therapy to lifestyle interventions for weight loss.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk for liver fibrosis (based on noninvasive tests), pioglitazone, a GLP-1 RA, or a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA is preferred for glycemic management because of potential beneficial effects on MASH.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk for liver fibrosis (based on noninvasive tests), metformin, a GLP-1 RA, or a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA is preferred for glycemic management because of potential beneficial effects on MASH.

correct: For diabetes, Combination therapy with pioglitazone plus GLP-1 RA can be considered for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk of liver fibrosis (identified with noninvasive tests) because of potential beneficial effects on MASH.
wrong: For diabetes, Combination therapy with glimepiride plus glyburide can be considered for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk of liver fibrosis (identified with noninvasive tests) because of potential beneficial effects on MASH.

correct: For diabetes, For consideration of treatment with a thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist in adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with MASLD with moderate (F2) or advanced (F3) liver fibrosis on liver histology, or by a validated imaging-based or blood-based test, refer to a gastroenterologist or hepatologist with expertise in MASLD management.
wrong: For diabetes, For consideration of treatment with a thyroid hormone receptor-α agonist in adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes with MASLD with moderate (F2) or advanced (F3) liver fibrosis on liver histology, or by a validated imaging-based or blood-based test, refer to a gastroenterologist or hepatologist with expertise in MASLD management.

correct: For diabetes, Provide weight management treatment based on nutrition, physical activity, and behavioral therapy for all people with overweight or obesity, aiming for at least 3–7% weight loss.
wrong: For diabetes, Provide weight management treatment based on nutrition, physical activity, and behavioral therapy for all people with overweight or obesity, aiming for at least 7–10% weight loss.

correct: For diabetes, Supplementation with micronutrients (e.g., vitamins and minerals, such as magnesium or chromium) or herbs or spices (e.g., cinnamon and aloe vera) for glycemic benefits is not recommended.
wrong: For diabetes, Health care professionals should inquire about intake of dietary supplements and counsel as necessary. Supplementation with micronutrients (e.g., vitamins and minerals, such as magnesium or chromium) or herbs or spices (e.g., cinnamon and aloe vera) for glycemic benefits is recommended.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes to limit sodium consumption to <2,300 mg/day, as clinically appropriate, and that the best way to achieve this is through limiting consumption of processed foods.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes to limit sodium consumption to <2,600 mg/day, as clinically appropriate, and that the best way to achieve this is through limiting consumption of processed foods.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel people with prediabetes and diabetes that water is recommended over nonnutritive sweetened beverages.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel people with prediabetes and diabetes that nonnutritive sweetened beverages may be an acceptable option.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes that nonnutritive sweeteners can be used instead of sugar-sweetened products if consumed in moderation and for the short term to reduce overall calorie and carbohydrate intake
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes that nonnutritive sweeteners can be used instead of sugar-sweetened products safely to reduce overall calorie and carbohydrate intake.

correct: For diabetes, Regardless of diabetes classification, individuals treated with sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors should avoid a ketogenic eating pattern, be educated on the signs of ketoacidosis and methods of risk mitigation and provided with appropriate tools for accurate ketone measurement (i.e., serum β-hydroxybutyrate), and be instructed to avoid fasting and maintain appropriate insulin therapy.
wrong: For diabetes, Regardless of diabetes classification, individuals treated with sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors should adopt a low-carbohydrate eating pattern, be educated on the signs of ketoacidosis and methods of risk mitigation, and provided with appropriate tools for accurate ketone measurement (i.e., serum β-hydroxybutyrate). They should monitor their caloric intake closely and maintain appropriate insulin therapy.

correct: For diabetes, People with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes are advised to incorporate more plant-based protein sources (e.g., nuts, seeds, and legumes) as part of an overall diverse eating pattern to reduce cardiovascular disease risk.
wrong: For diabetes, People with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes are advised to incorporate more animal-based protein sources (e.g., lean meats, fish, and poultry) as part of an overall diverse eating pattern to reduce cardiovascular disease risk.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to limit intake of foods high in saturated fat (e.g., red meat, full-fat dairy, butter, and coconut oil) to help reduce cardiovascular disease risk.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes and those at risk for diabetes to limit intake of foods high in fat to help reduce cardiovascular disease risk.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes that prolonged sitting should be interrupted at least every 30 min for blood glucose benefits.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel people with diabetes that prolonged sitting should be interrupted at least every 60 minutes for blood glucose benefits.

correct: For diabetes, Counsel adults and youth treated with weight management pharmacotherapy or metabolic surgery that meeting physical activity recommendations, and in particular muscle-strengthening exercises, may be beneficial for maintaining lean body mass.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel adults and youth treated with weight management pharmacotherapy or metabolic surgery that avoiding muscle-strengthening exercises may be beneficial for maintaining lean body mass.

correct: For diabetes, Advise people with type 1 diabetes and those with other forms of diabetes at risk for diabetic ketoacidosis not to use recreational cannabis in any form.
wrong: For diabetes, Advise people with type 1 diabetes and those with other forms of diabetes at risk for diabetic ketoacidosis to avoid recreational cannabis unless administered in controlled, low-dose regimens.

correct: For diabetes, Weight management pharmacotherapy indicated for chronic therapy should be continued beyond reaching weight loss goals to maintain the health benefits. Sudden discontinuation of weight management pharmacotherapy often results in weight gain and worsening of cardiometabolic risk factors.
wrong: For diabetes, Weight management pharmacotherapy indicated for chronic therapy should be discontinued once weight loss goals are achieved to prevent the risk of long-term side effects. Prolonged use of weight management pharmacotherapy often results in tolerance and diminished efficacy.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and established or high risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, the treatment plan should include medications with demonstrated benefits to reduce cardiovascular events (e.g., glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist [GLP-1 RA] and/or sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 [SGLT2] inhibitor) for glycemic management and comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction (irrespective of A1C)
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and established or high risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, the treatment plan should include medications with demonstrated benefits to reduce cardiovascular events (e.g., dipeptidyl peptidase-4 [DPP-4] inhibitor and/or metformin) for glycemic management and comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction (irrespective of A1C).

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes who have heart failure (HF) (with either reduced or preserved ejection fraction), an SGLT2 inhibitor is recommended for both glycemic management and prevention of HF hospitalizations (irrespective of A1C)
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes who have heart failure (HF) (with either reduced or preserved ejection fraction), a DPP-4 inhibitor is recommended for both glycemic management and prevention of HF hospitalizations (irrespective of A1C).

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity, a GLP-1 RA with demonstrated benefits for both glycemic management and reduction of HF-related symptoms (irrespective of A1C) is recommended
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity, a DPP-4 inhibitor with demonstrated benefits for both glycemic management and reduction of HF-related symptoms (irrespective of A1C) is recommended.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes who have CKD (with confirmed estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] 20–60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and/or albuminuria), an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA with demonstrated benefit in this population should be used for both glycemic management (irrespective of A1C) and for slowing progression of CKD and reduction in cardiovascular events. The glycemic benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors are reduced at eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m2.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes who have CKD (with confirmed estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] 10–50 mL/min/1.73 m2 and/or albuminuria), an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA with demonstrated benefit in this population should be used for both glycemic management (irrespective of A1C) and for slowing progression of CKD and reduction in cardiovascular events. The glycemic benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors are reduced at eGFR <35 mL/min/1.73 m2.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and overweight or obesity, consider using a GLP-1 RA or a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 RA with potential benefits in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH) for glycemic management and as an adjunctive to healthy interventions for weight loss.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and overweight or obesity, consider using a DPP-4 inhibitor or a combination of a sulfonylurea and thiazolidinedione for potential benefits in MASH for glycemic management and as an adjunctive to healthy interventions for weight loss.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk for liver fibrosis (based on noninvasive tests), pioglitazone, a GLP-1 RA, or a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA is preferred for glycemic management due to potential beneficial effects on MASH.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk for liver fibrosis (based on noninvasive tests), metformin, a DPP-4 inhibitor, or a sulfonylurea is preferred for glycemic management due to potential beneficial effects on MASH.

correct: For diabetes, Combination therapy with pioglitazone plus a GLP-1 RA can be considered for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes with biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk of liver fibrosis (identified with noninvasive tests) due to potential beneficial effects on MASH.
wrong: For diabetes, The use of pioglitazone in combination with a GLP-1 RA for the treatment of hyperglycemia in adults with type 2 diabetes and biopsy-proven MASH or those at high risk of liver fibrosis (identified with noninvasive tests) is not recommended due to insufficient evidence of beneficial effects on MASH.

correct: For diabetes, When initiating a new glucose-lowering medication, reassess the need for and/or dose of medications with higher hypoglycemia risk (i.e., sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and insulin) to minimize the risk of hypoglycemia and treatment burden.
wrong: For diabetes, When initiating a new glucose-lowering medication, adjustment of medications with higher hypoglycemia risk (i.e., sulfonylureas, meglitinides, and insulin) is generally not necessary.

correct: For diabetes, Concurrent use of dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitors with a GLP-1 RA or a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA is not recommended due to lack of additional glucose lowering beyond that of a GLP-1 RA alone.
wrong: For diabetes, Concurrent use of dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitors with a GLP-1 RA or a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA may be considered due to potential additional glucose-lowering benefits.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes and no evidence of insulin deficiency, a GLP-1 RA, including a dual GIP and GLP-1 RA, is preferred to insulin
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with type 2 diabetes without insulin deficiency, no single option, whether GLP-1 receptor agonists, DPP-4 inhibitors, or insulin, is preferred over the others. Treatment should be individualized.

correct: For diabetes, Do not use basal insulin doses exceeding 0.5 units/kg/day as evidence of overbasalization. Instead, identify overbasalization based on significant bedtime-to-morning or postprandial-to-preprandial glucose differentials, hypoglycemia (aware or unaware), and high glycemic variability.
wrong: For diabetes, Basal insulin doses exceeding 0.5 units/kg/day should be considered evidence of overbasalization.

correct: For diabetes, Educate individuals with diabetes who are at risk for developing diabetic ketoacidosis and/or follow a ketogenic eating pattern and who are treated with SGLT inhibitors on the risks and signs of ketoacidosis and methods of risk mitigation management, and provide them with appropriate tools for accurate ketone measurement (i.e., serum β-hydroxybutyrate).
wrong: For diabetes, Educate individuals with diabetes who are at risk for developing diabetic ketoacidosis and/or follow a ketogenic eating pattern and who are treated with SGLT inhibitors on the risks and signs of ketoacidosis and methods of risk mitigation management, and provide them with appropriate tools for ketone measurement (i.e., urine dipstick).

correct: For diabetes, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, MRAs, direct renin inhibitors, and neprilysin inhibitors should be avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception and are contraindicated in pregnancy.
wrong: For diabetes, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, MRAs, direct renin inhibitors, and neprilysin inhibitors are generally safe for use in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential when reliable contraception is employed.

correct: For diabetes, In most circumstances, lipid-lowering agents should be stopped prior to conception and avoided in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential who are not using reliable contraception.
wrong: For diabetes, In most circumstances, lipid-lowering agents should be carefully monitored prior to conception and used cautiously in sexually active individuals of childbearing potential.

correct: For diabetes, In some circumstances, such as for sexually active individuals of childbearing potential with familial hypercholesterolemia or a prior ASCVD event, statin therapy may be continued when the benefits outweigh the risks.
wrong: For diabetes, In some circumstances, such as for sexually active individuals of childbearing potential with familial hypercholesterolemia or a prior ASCVD event, statin therapy need to be avoided due to potential risks.

correct: For diabetes, In adults with hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides >150 mg/dL [>1.7 mmol/L] or nonfasting triglycerides >175 mg/dL [>2.0 mmol/L]), clinicians should address and treat lifestyle factors (obesity and metabolic syndrome), secondary factors (diabetes, chronic liver or kidney disease and/or nephrotic syndrome, and hypothyroidism), and medications that raise triglycerides.
wrong: For diabetes, In adults with hypertriglyceridemia (fasting triglycerides >140 mg/dL [>1.6 mmol/L] or nonfasting triglycerides >165 mg/dL [>1.9 mmol/L]), clinicians should address and treat lifestyle factors (obesity and metabolic syndrome), secondary factors (diabetes, chronic liver or kidney disease and/or nephrotic syndrome, and hypothyroidism), and medications that raise triglycerides.

correct: For diabetes, In individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (150–499 mg/dL [1.7–5.6 mmol/L]), the addition of icosapent ethyl can be considered to reduce cardiovascular risk.
wrong: For diabetes, In individuals with ASCVD or other cardiovascular risk factors on a statin with managed LDL cholesterol but elevated triglycerides (140–499 mg/dL [1.6–5.9 mmol/L]), the addition of icosapent ethyl can be considered to reduce cardiovascular risk.

correct: For diabetes, In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥65 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management.
wrong: For diabetes, In asymptomatic individuals with diabetes and age ≥55 years, microvascular disease in any location, or foot complications or any end-organ damage from diabetes, screening for PAD with ankle-brachial index testing is recommended if a PAD diagnosis would change management.

correct: For diabetes, In individuals with diabetes duration ≥10 years and high cardiovascular risk, screening for PAD should be considered.
wrong: For diabetes, In individuals with diabetes duration ≥8 years and low cardiovascular risk, screening for PAD should be considered.

correct: For diabetes, In individuals with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, therapy with a GLP-1 RA with demonstrated benefit for reduction of heart failure–related symptoms, physical limitations, and exercise function is recommended.
wrong: For diabetes, In individuals with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, therapy with a GLP-1 RA for the reduction of heart failure–related symptoms, physical limitations, and exercise function is not recommended due to insufficient evidence.

correct: For diabetes, To reduce cardiovascular risk and kidney disease progression in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD, a glucagon-like peptide 1 agonist with demonstrated benefit in this population is recommended.
wrong: For diabetes, To reduce cardiovascular risk and kidney disease progression in people with type 2 diabetes and CKD, the use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 agonist is not recommended due to unclear evidence of benefit in this population.

correct: For diabetes, Aim to reduce urinary albumin by ≥30% in people with CKD and albuminuria ≥300 mg/g to slow CKD progression.
wrong: For diabetes, Aim to reduce urinary albumin by ≥24% in people with CKD and albuminuria ≥275 mg/g to slow CKD progression.

correct: For diabetes, For people with non–dialysis-dependent stage G3 or higher CKD, protein intake should be 0.8 g/kg body weight per day.
wrong: For diabetes, For people with non–dialysis-dependent stage G3 or higher CKD, protein intake should be 0.65 g/kg body weight per day.

correct: For diabetes, For individuals on dialysis, protein intake of 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day should be considered since protein energy wasting is a major problem for some individuals on dialysis.
wrong: For diabetes, For individuals on dialysis, protein intake of 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day should be considered as protein energy wasting is a major problem for some individuals on dialysis.

correct: For diabetes, In a patient with both chronic kidney disease and type 1 diabetes, nondiabetic kidney disease should be considered if the diabetes duration is less than 5 years.
wrong: For diabetes, In a patient with both chronic kidney disease and type 1 diabetes, nondiabetic kidney disease should be considered if the diabetes duration is less than 10 years.

correct: For diabetes, Active urine sediment, such as red blood cells or cellular casts, is a reason to consider NONDIABETIC kidney disease in patients who have both diabetes and chronic kidney disease.
wrong: For diabetes, Active urine sediment, such as red blood cells or cellular casts, is indicative of diabetic kidney disease progression in patients with diabetes and chronic kidney disease.

correct: For diabetes, When a patient with chronic kidney disease and diabetes has chronically well-managed blood glucose, clinicians should consider the possibility of a nondiabetic cause for their kidney disease.
wrong: For diabetes, When a patient with chronic kidney disease and diabetes has chronically well-managed blood glucose, clinicians may be less likely to consider the possibility of a nondiabetic cause for their kidney disease.

correct: For diabetes, Rapidly declining eGFR in a patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease should prompt evaluation for nondiabetic kidney disease etiology.
wrong: For diabetes, Rapidly declining eGFR in a patient with diabetes and chronic kidney disease is consistent with diabetic nephropathy progression and does not typically warrant evaluation for nondiabetic kidney disease etiologies.

correct: For diabetes, Consider nondiabetic causes of kidney disease when a patient with diabetes and CKD presents with rapidly increasing or very high UACR or urine protein/creatinine levels.
wrong: For diabetes, Consider diabetic nephropathy as the primary cause of kidney disease in a patient with diabetes and CKD presenting with rapidly increasing or very high UACR or urine protein/creatinine levels.

correct: For diabetes, The absence of retinopathy in a person with type 1 diabetes who has chronic kidney disease suggests possible nondiabetic kidney disease etiology.
wrong: For diabetes, The absence of retinopathy in a person with type 1 diabetes who has chronic kidney disease suggests that the kidney disease is likely of diabetic etiology.

correct: For diabetes, Blood glucose management is an effective intervention for lowering albuminuria in patients with kidney disease.
wrong: For diabetes, Intensive glycemic control may be beneficial in early stages of diabetic nephropathy but has limited evidence for established kidney disease. For non-diabetic kidney disease patients, glucose management should not be considered a primary intervention for albuminuria reduction.

correct: For diabetes, Blood pressure management should be implemented to reduce albuminuria levels.
wrong: For diabetes, Blood pressure management should be implemented to reduce albuminuria levels, but only in patients with confirmed hypertension.

correct: For diabetes, Treatment with ACE inhibitors or ARBs is recommended to lower albuminuria in patients with kidney disease.
wrong: For diabetes, ACE inhibitors or ARBs should be used cautiously to control albuminuria in patients with kidney disease.

correct: For diabetes, Smoking cessation is an important intervention that can help reduce albuminuria levels.
wrong: For diabetes, Smoking cessation is a POTENTIAL intervention for patients with albuminuria, though there is no evidence to demonstrate it reduces albuminuria levels.

correct: For diabetes, Dietary modifications, including decreased salt intake and/or protein intake, can effectively lower albuminuria.
wrong: For diabetes, Dietary modifications, including decreased salt intake and/or protein intake, may provide limited effect in reducing albuminuria.

correct: For diabetes, Treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors, MRAs, or GLP-1 receptor agonists should be considered for lowering albuminuria in patients with kidney disease.
wrong: For diabetes, Treatment with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or diuretics should be considered for lowering albuminuria in patients with kidney disease.

correct: For diabetes, Opioids, including tramadol and tapentadol, should not be used for neuropathic pain treatment in diabetes given the potential for adverse events.
wrong: For diabetes, Opioids, such as tramadol and tapentadol, are generally not recommended for the management of neuropathic pain in diabetic patients, but they may be considered in patients with established opioid tolerance.

correct: For diabetes, Refer individuals who smoke and have a history of prior lower-extremity complications, loss of protective sensation, structural abnormalities, or PAD to foot care specialists for ongoing preventive care and lifelong surveillance.
wrong: For diabetes, Refer individuals who smoke and have a history of prior lower-extremity complications, loss of protective sensation, or structural abnormalities to foot care specialists for short-term monitoring and preventive care.

correct: For diabetes, Consider age-approved statins, in addition to MNT and lifestyle changes, for youth with type 1 diabetes who have LDL cholesterol ≥130 mg/dL (≥3.4 mmol/L).
wrong: For diabetes, Consider age-approved statins, in addition to MNT and lifestyle changes, for youth with type 1 diabetes who have LDL cholesterol ≥120 mg/dL (≥3.1 mmol/L).

correct: For diabetes, Consider setting an A1C goal of <6.5% (<48 mmol/mol) for most children and adolescents with type 2 diabetes who have a low risk of hypoglycemia.
wrong: For diabetes, Consider setting an A1C goal of <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol) for most children and adolescents with type 2 diabetes who have a low risk of hypoglycemia.

correct: For diabetes, Individuals presenting with severe hyperglycemia (blood glucose ≥600 mg/dL [≥33.3 mmol/L]), consider assessment for hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state.
wrong: For diabetes, Individuals presenting with severe hyperglycemia (blood glucose ≥550 mg/dL [≥30.6 mmol/L]), consider assessment for hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state.

correct: For diabetes, Electronic cigarette use or vaping should be discouraged.
wrong: For diabetes, For adults with established smoking habits, electronic cigarettes may be considered as a short-term smoking cessation aid under supervision.

correct: For diabetes, Advise all youth with diabetes not to use cannabis recreationally in any form.
wrong: For diabetes, Counsel youth with diabetes to avoid recreational cannabis except when they have stable blood glucose levels and are under supervision.

correct: For diabetes, A folic acid supplement of 400–800 μg/day is recommended as part of preconception care for people with prediabetes, diabetes, or a history of gestational diabetes mellitus.
wrong: For diabetes, A folic acid supplement of 600-1000 μg/day is recommended as part of preconception care for people with prediabetes, diabetes, or a history of gestational diabetes mellitus.

correct: For diabetes, Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems with pregnancy-specific glucose targets are recommended for pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes.
wrong: For diabetes, Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems are contraindicated for pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes. Conventional insulin pump therapy with manual adjustments and regular blood glucose monitoring remains the standard of care during pregnancy.

correct: For diabetes, AID systems without pregnancy-specific glucose targets or a pregnancy-specific algorithm may be considered for select pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes when used with assistive techniques and working with experienced health care teams.
wrong: For diabetes, AID systems without pregnancy-specific glucose targets or a pregnancy-specific algorithm should not be used for pregnant individuals with type 1 diabetes.

correct: For diabetes, Metformin and glyburide, individually or in combination, should not be used as first-line agents for management of diabetes in pregnancy, as both cross the placenta to the fetus A and may not be sufficient to achieve glycemic goals.
wrong: For diabetes, Metformin and glyburide, individually or in combination, are appropriate first-line agents for management of diabetes in pregnancy and can be used in certain contexts. Both agents cross the placenta to the fetus, and their use may require monitoring to ensure adequate glycemic control.

correct: For diabetes, Other oral and noninsulin injectable glucose-lowering medications are not recommended for management of diabetes in pregnancy.
wrong: For diabetes, oral and noninsulin injectable glucose-lowering medications may be considered for management of diabetes in pregnancy.

correct: For diabetes, Insulin should be initiated or intensified for treatment of persistent hyperglycemia starting at a threshold of ≥180 mg/dL (≥10.0 mmol/L) (confirmed on two occasions within 24 h) for the majority of critically ill individuals (those in the intensive care unit [ICU]).
wrong: For diabetes, Insulin and/or other glucose-lowering therapies should be initiated or intensified for treatment of persistent hyperglycemia starting at a threshold of ≥170 mg/dL (≥9.4 mmol/L) (confirmed on two occasions within 36 h) for the majority of noncritically ill individuals (those not in the ICU).

correct: For diabetes, Insulin and/or other glucose-lowering therapies should be initiated or intensified for treatment of persistent hyperglycemia starting at a threshold of ≥180 mg/dL (≥10.0 mmol/L) (confirmed on two occasions within 24 h) for the majority of noncritically ill individuals (those not in the ICU).
wrong: For diabetes, Insulin and/or other glucose-lowering therapies should be initiated or intensified for treatment of persistent hyperglycemia starting at a threshold of ≥170 mg/dL (≥9.4 mmol/L) (confirmed on two occasions within 36 h) for the majority of noncritically ill individuals (those not in the ICU).

correct: For diabetes, Once therapy is initiated, a glycemic goal of 140–180 mg/dL (7.8–10.0 mmol/L) is recommended for most critically ill individuals (those in the ICU) with hyperglycemia. A More stringent individualized glycemic goals may be appropriate for selected critically ill individuals if they can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia.
wrong: For diabetes, Once therapy is initiated, a glycemic goal of 160-200 mg/dL (8.9-11.1 mmol/L) is recommended for most critically ill individuals (those in the ICU) with hyperglycemia. More stringent individualized glycemic goals may be appropriate for selected critically ill individuals if they can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia.

correct: For diabetes, For noncritically ill individuals (those not in the ICU), a glycemic goal of 100–180 mg/dL (5.6-10.0 mmol/L) is recommended if it can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia.
wrong: For diabetes, For noncritically ill individuals (those not in the ICU), a glycemic goal of 120–200 mg/dL (6.7-11.1 mmol/L) is recommended if it can be achieved without significant hypoglycemia.

correct: For diabetes, Continuous intravenous insulin infusion is recommended for achieving glycemic goals and avoiding hypoglycemia in critically ill individuals.
wrong: For diabetes, Continuous intravenous insulin infusion may not be appropriate for achieving glycemic goals and avoiding hypoglycemia in critically ill individuals.

correct: For diabetes, Manage diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) by administering intravenous fluids, insulin, and electrolytes and by closely monitoring during treatment, ensuring timely and bridged transition to maintenance subcutaneous insulin administration, and identifying and treating the precipitating cause.
wrong: For diabetes, Manage diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state (HHS) by administering oral fluids, metformin, and potassium supplements, and by closely monitoring during treatment, ensuring timely transition to maintenance metformin administration, and identifying and treating the precipitating cause.

correct: For diabetes, Health systems should adopt a culture of quality improvement, implement benchmarking programs, and engage interprofessional teams to support sustainable and scalable process changes to improve quality of care and health outcomes.
wrong: For diabetes, Health systems should prioritize adherence to standardized protocols and maintain existing care delivery structures to ensure reliability across clinical settings.

correct: For diabetes, Health systems should assess and address disparities in diabetes care and health outcomes (e.g., by stratifying clinical quality data by factors such as insurance status, race, ethnicity, preferred language for health care discussions, disability, and other social determinants of health).
wrong: For diabetes, Health systems should aim to provide uniform diabetes care protocols to all patients to ensure consistency and fairness in treatment delivery.

correct: For diabetes, Classify people with hyperglycemia into appropriate diagnostic categories to aid in personalized management.
wrong: For diabetes, Manage individuals with hyperglycemia using general treatment protocols to ensure consistent care across populations.

correct: For diabetes, Individuals with a history of GDM should have lifelong screening for the development of prediabetes or diabetes at least every 3 years.
wrong: For diabetes, Individuals with a history of GDM should undergo long-term screening for the development of prediabetes or diabetes, at least every 3 years for a total duration of 9 years.

correct: For HIV, People with HIV should be managed by a multidisciplinary team before, during, and after transplant.
wrong: For HIV, People with HIV should be managed by a single specialist before, during, and after transplant.

correct: For HIV, Transplant candidates with HIV should be up-to-date on their vaccination schedule
wrong: For HIV, Transplant candidates with HIV should avoid vaccinations due to potential immune system complications.

correct: For HIV, Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) is preferred over tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in transplant candidates and recipients due to the lower risk of affecting renal function and bone mineral density.
wrong: For HIV, Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) is preferred over tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) in transplant candidates and recipients due to the lower risk of affecting renal function and bone mineral density.

correct: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, unboosted second-generation oral integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based regimens (specifically bictegravir or dolutegravir) are preferred in most cases to avoid significant drug-drug interactions.
wrong: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, boosted protease inhibitor (PI)-based regimens (specifically darunavir/ritonavir or atazanavir/ritonavir) are preferred in most cases due to their high genetic barrier to resistance and established clinical experience.

correct: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, potent cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4 inhibitors—including pharmacokinetic boosters such as ritonavir (RTV) or cobicistat (COBI), and protease inhibitor (PI)-containing regimens should generally be avoided to prevent significant drug-drug interactions.
wrong: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, potent cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4 inhibitors—including pharmacokinetic boosters such as ritonavir (RTV) or cobicistat (COBI), and protease inhibitor (PI)-containing regimens should be used with careful monitoring and dose adjustments of concomitant medications to manage potential drug-drug interactions.

correct: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as nevirapine (NVP), efavirenz (EFV), and etravirine (ETR), which are CYP3A4 inducers—should generally be avoided to prevent significant drug-drug interactions.
wrong: For HIV, For transplant candidates with HIV, non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs) such as nevirapine (NVP), efavirenz (EFV), and etravirine (ETR), which are CYP3A4 inducers may be considered with caution to minimize potential drug-drug interactions.

correct: For HIV, Immediately post-transplant, renal or hepatic function may fluctuate; close monitoring of these organ functions is recommended to ensure appropriate dosing of ARV drugs and other concomitant medications to avoid potential drug toxicities.
wrong: For HIV, Immediately post-transplant, renal or hepatic function is generally stable; routine monitoring of these organ functions is advised to ensure appropriate dosing of ARV drugs and other concomitant medications to prevent potential drug toxicities.

correct: For HIV, Interruption of antiretroviral therapy (ART) post-transplant should be avoided.
wrong: For HIV, Interruption of antiretroviral therapy (ART) post-transplant may be considered, but should be minimized whenever possible.

correct: For HIV, If ART interruption becomes necessary in the immediate post-transplant period, stop all components of an oral ART regimen simultaneously to prevent exposure to an incomplete regimen.
wrong: For HIV, If ART interruption becomes necessary in the immediate post-transplant period, consider a staggered discontinuation based on the half-lives of the individual components to minimize the risk of resistance development.

correct: For HIV, When ART interruption occurs in the immediate post-transplant period, the duration of interruption should be kept to a minimum.
wrong: For HIV, When ART interruption occurs in the post-transplant period, resumption should be considered once the patient demonstrates stable graft function and adequate absorption of oral medications.

correct: For HIV, Transplant recipients with active HBV infection should be treated with ARV regimens with anti-HBV activity before transplant and indefinitely after transplant.
wrong: For HIV, Transplant recipients with active HBV infection should be treated with ARV regimens before transplant and continue treatment for at least 24 months after transplant, with consideration for indefinite therapy based on periodic HBV viral load monitoring.

correct: For HIV, Use of nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) with activities against both HIV and HBV is strongly recommended unless contraindicated or not tolerated.
wrong: For HIV, Use of nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) with activities against both HIV and HBV may be considered as a treatment option unless contraindicated or not tolerated.

correct: For HIV, Because of the current low rates of transmitted INSTI resistance in the United States, even when there is suspicion that HIV was acquired from a partner with virologic failure while on an INSTI, an INSTI-based regimen can be started pending the results of the INSTI genotype.
wrong: For HIV, Due to concerns about potential transmitted INSTI resistance in the United States, when there is suspicion that HIV was acquired from a partner with virologic failure while on an INSTI, it is recommended to avoid starting an INSTI-based regimen until the results of the INSTI genotype are available.

correct: For HIV, Dolutegravir (DTG) combined with abacavir and lamivudine (3TC) is no longer recommended as an initial regimen for most people with HIV. This decision is based on the requirement for HLA-B*5701 testing prior to initiation, concerns about a possible increased risk of cardiovascular events, and the availability of other well-tolerated and effective treatment options.
wrong: For HIV, Dolutegravir (DTG) combined with abacavir and lamivudine (3TC) is recommended as an initial regimen for most people with HIV. This decision is based on the requirement for HLA-B*5701 testing prior to initiation, the low risk of cardiovascular events, and the availability of other well-tolerated and effective treatment options.

correct: For HIV, Dolutegravir (DTG) in combination with abacavir and lamivudine (3TC) may be considered as an initial regimen in specific clinical scenarios. It is now listed among the alternative options for initial antiretroviral therapy in certain contexts.
wrong: For HIV, Dolutegravir (DTG) in combination with abacavir and lamivudine (3TC) is not recommended as an initial regimen in specific clinical scenarios.

correct: For HIV, When concern about renal- or bone-associated AEs precludes the use of TDF or TAF, would recommend using DTG/ABC/3TC (if HLA-B*5701-negative).
wrong: For HIV, When concern about renal- or bone-associated AEs precludes the use of TDF, would recommend using EFV/ABC/3TC or RAL/ABC/3TC.

correct: For HIV, For people who previously received long-acting (LA) cabotegravir (CAB) plus rilpivirine (RPV), or LA-CAB/RPV, and present with virologic failure, resistance testing (including integrase strand transfer inhibitor INSTI genotypic testing) should be performed regardless of the time since the last dose of LA CAB/RPV.
wrong: For HIV, For people who previously received long-acting (LA) cabotegravir (CAB) plus rilpivirine (RPV), or LA-CAB/RPV, and present with virologic failure, resistance testing (including integrase strand transfer inhibitor INSTI genotypic testing) should be performed if the failure occurs within 12 weeks of the last dose of LA CAB/RPV.

correct: For HIV, Intramuscular (IM) injections in the buttock should be avoided in areas where gluteal implants or soft tissue fillers are present
wrong: For HIV, Intramuscular (IM) injections in the buttock may be performed with caution in areas where gluteal implants or soft tissue fillers are present, provided proper anatomical landmarks are identified and the injection is administered at least 2 cm away from the implant or filler margins.

correct: For HIV, Lenacapavir (LEN) is now recognized as an antiretroviral (ARV) agent that may increase concentrations of certain gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) medications.
wrong: For HIV, Lenacapavir (LEN) is not known to significantly affect concentrations of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) medications and routine dose adjustments are generally not necessary.

correct: For HIV, Adefovir (AI) or pegylated interferon alfa are not recommended for people with HBV/HIV coinfection.
wrong: For HIV, Adefovir (AI) or pegylated interferon alfa can be considered as alternative options for select patients with HBV/HIV coinfection.

correct: For HIV, Pegylated interferon should only be considered in rare cases and with consultation with an expert in HBV.
wrong: For HIV, Pegylated interferon is recommended for eligible HBV patients.

correct: For HIV, All people with HIV should be tested for viral hepatitis, including hepatitis A virus (HAV), HBV, and hepatitis C virus (HCV).
wrong: For HIV, All people with HIV should be tested for viral hepatitis, including hepatitis A virus (HAV), HBV, and hepatitis C virus (HCV), except those with CD4 counts consistently above 500 cells/mm³ who report no history of injection drug use or high-risk sexual behavior.

correct: For HIV, People without immunity to HAV or HBV should receive a full vaccination series.
wrong: For HIV, People at high risk for HAV or HBV exposure may consider vaccination, preferably starting with HBV which carries higher morbidity.

correct: For HIV, For a person with virologic suppression while on a DTG 50 mg once-daily regimen, the DTG dose should be increased to 50 mg twice daily throughout the course of 1HP, continuing DTG 50 mg twice daily for 14 days after 1HP completion before switching back to once-daily DTG dosing.
wrong: For HIV, For a person with virologic suppression while on a DTG 50 mg once-daily regimen, the DTG dose should be increased to 50 mg twice daily throughout the course of 1HP, continuing DTG 50 mg twice daily for 12 days after 1HP completion before switching back to once-daily DTG dosing.

correct: For HIV, Initiate ART after TB meningitis is under control and after at least 2 weeks of anti-TB treatment to reduce the risk of life-threatening inflammation in a closed space as a result of immune reconstitution.
wrong: For HIV, Initiate ART after TB meningitis is under control and after at least 10 days of anti-TB treatment to reduce the risk of life-threatening inflammation in a closed space as a result of immune reconstitution.

correct: For HIV, The preferred vaccine in previously unvaccinated patients is Heplisav-B given at 0 and 4 weeks.
wrong: For HIV, The preferred vaccine in previously unvaccinated patients is Heplisav-B given at 0, and 32 days.

correct: For HIV, In those who failed a prior vaccine series with Engerix-B or Recombivax HB, Heplisav-B at 0 and 4 weeks is recommended
wrong: For HIV, In those who failed a prior vaccine series with Engerix-B or Recombivax HB, Heplisav-B at 0 and 32 days is recommended

correct: For HIV, Isavuconazole sulfate is one of the alternative treatments for mild-to-moderate pulmonary infections.
wrong: For HIV, Isavuconazole sulfate is the preferred first-line treatment for mild-to-moderate pulmonary infections.

correct: For HIV, Pegylated interferon (IFN)-α-2a (or 2b) monotherapy may be used for the treatment of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection only in rare clinical circumstances and should be prescribed in consultation with a specialist.
wrong: For HIV, Pegylated interferon (IFN)-α-2a (or 2b) monotherapy is recommended as a treatment option for eligible patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection.

correct: For HIV, In severely ill patients requiring empiric parenteral therapy while awaiting susceptibility, initiate a carbapenem until antimicrobial susceptibilities are available
wrong: For HIV, In severely ill patients requiring empiric parenteral therapy while awaiting susceptibility, initiate a third-generation cephalosporin until antimicrobial susceptibilities are available

correct: For HIV, For people with HIV and severe disease, with clinically severe diarrhea, if Campylobacter or Shigella bacteremia is suspected, a carbapenem is preferred for empiric therapy
wrong: For HIV, For people with HIV and severe disease, with clinically severe diarrhea, if Campylobacter or Shigella bacteremia is suspected, a fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin) is preferred for empiric therapy.

correct: For HIV, Administration of a single respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine (Abrysvo, Arexvy, or mRESVIA) to all people with HIV >75 years old is recommended
wrong: For HIV, Administration of a single respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine (Abrysvo, Arexvy, or mRESVIA) to all people with HIV >75 years old is not routinely recommended.

correct: For HIV, Treatment of patients with coccidioidal meningitis: Fluconazole (800 to 1,200 mg daily) is the preferred regimen.
wrong: For HIV, Treatment of patients with coccidioidal meningitis: Fluconazole (600 to 1,000 mg daily) is the preferred regimen.

correct: For HIV, Pneumocystis pneumonia primary prophylaxis should be initiated in people with HIV who have CD4 counts of 100–200 cells/mm³ if their plasma HIV RNA level is above detection limits.
wrong: For HIV, Pneumocystis pneumonia primary prophylaxis should be initiated in people with HIV who have CD4 counts of 80–180 cells/mm³ if their plasma HIV RNA level is above detection limits.

correct: For HIV, Pneumocystis pneumonia primary prophylaxis should also be initiated in people with HIV who have CD4 counts <100 cells/mm³, regardless of their plasma HIV RNA level.
wrong: For HIV, Pneumocystis pneumonia primary prophylaxis should also be initiated in people with HIV who have CD4 counts <110 cells/mm³, regardless of their plasma HIV RNA level.

correct: For HIV, When acute HIV infection is suspected during pregnancy or the intrapartum period or while breastfeeding, a plasma HIV RNA assay should be performed in conjunction with an antigen/antibody immunoassay.
wrong: For HIV, When acute HIV infection is suspected during pregnancy or the intrapartum period or while breastfeeding, an antigen/antibody immunoassay should be performed.

correct: For HIV, For postpartum people at increased risk of HIV acquisition, HIV testing and PrEP should be offered. If the parent is breastfeeding, consult an HIV specialist regarding frequency of HIV testing for the breastfeeding parent and/or infant.
wrong: For HIV, For postpartum mothers at risk of HIV acquisition, HIV testing should be offered. PrEP is generally not recommended during the postpartum period due to limited safety data.

correct: For HIV, One FDA-approved antigen/antibody test can be performed at the point of care (POC), provides results after 20 minutes, and must be read before 30 minutes.
wrong: For HIV, One FDA-approved antigen/antibody test can be performed at the point of care (POC), provides results after 30 minutes, and must be read before 40 minutes.

correct: For HIV, If the repeat parental viral load is undetectable, a joint decision should be made by the parent and providers about whether breastfeeding may resume.
wrong: For HIV, If the repeat parental viral load is undetectable, breastfeeding should still be avoided as the risk of HIV transmission cannot be completely eliminated even with suppressed viral loads.

correct: For HIV, Pediatricians should be prepared to offer a family centered, nonjudgmental, harm reduction approach to support people with HIV on ART with sustained viral suppression below 50 copies per mL who desire to breastfeed.
wrong: For HIV, Pediatricians should be prepared to offer a family centered, nonjudgmental, harm reduction approach to support people with HIV on ART with sustained viral suppression below 60 copies per mL who desire to breastfeed.

correct: For HIV, Virologic diagnostic testing using an HIV NAT is recommended for all infants with perinatal HIV exposure.
wrong: For HIV, Virologic diagnostic testing using an HIV NAT is recommended for symptomatic infants with confirmed perinatal HIV exposure after 18 months of age.

correct: For HIV, The test at birth generally should be performed in all infants with perinatal HIV exposure but is not necessary for infants at low risk of HIV acquisition (defined as being born to a person who had HIV RNA levels <50 copies/mL
wrong: For HIV, The test at birth generally should be performed in all infants with perinatal HIV exposure but is not necessary for infants at low risk of HIV acquisition (defined as being born to a person who had HIV RNA levels <100 copies/mL

correct: For HIV, For infants who receive presumptive HIV therapy, additional virologic diagnostic testing is recommended 2 to 6 weeks after antiretroviral (ARV) drugs are discontinued.
wrong: For HIV, For infants who receive presumptive HIV therapy, additional virologic diagnostic testing is recommended 4 to 8 weeks after antiretroviral (ARV) drugs are discontinued.

correct: For HIV, Virologic diagnostic testing should be performed at least every 3 months during breastfeeding.
wrong: For HIV, Virologic diagnostic testing should be performed at least every 3 weeks during breastfeeding.

correct: For HIV, For children aged ≥18 months, HIV antibody (or HIV antigen/antibody) tests are recommended for diagnostic testing.
wrong: For HIV, For all children (aged ≥0 months), HIV antibody (or HIV antigen/antibody) tests are recommended for diagnostic testing.

correct: For HIV, Diagnosis in children aged ≥18 months relies primarily on HIV antibody and antigen/antibody tests.
wrong: For HIV, Diagnosis in children aged ≥18 months relies primarily on clinical symptoms and CD4 count monitoring.

correct: For HIV, Baseline screening for tuberculosis should be performed, including a tuberculin skin test for children aged ≥18 months.
wrong: For HIV, Baseline screening for tuberculosis should be performed, including a tuberculin skin test for children aged ≥12 months.

correct: For HIV, Baseline screening for cytomegalovirus (CMV) should be performed, including CMV antibody testing for children aged >12 months.
wrong: For HIV, Baseline screening for cytomegalovirus (CMV) should be performed, including CMV antibody testing for children aged >6 months.

correct: For HIV, Baseline hepatitis C screening is recommended with HCV nucleic acid (HCV RNA) testing if aged <18 months or Hepatitis C antibody if aged ≥18 months
wrong: For HIV, Baseline hepatitis C screening is recommended with HCV nucleic acid (HCV RNA) testing if aged <16 months or Hepatitis C antibody if aged ≥16 months

correct: For HIV, ART initiation should be discussed and strongly encouraged at every visit.
wrong: For HIV, ART initiation may be discussed at every visit.

correct: For HIV, Term infants (≥37 weeks gestation) or preterm infants with a postmenstrual age ≥37 weeks at the time of treatment initiation should receive NVP plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC, or RAL (for infants weighing ≥2 kg) plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC.
wrong: For HIV, Term infants (≥42 weeks gestation) or preterm infants with a postmenstrual age ≥42 weeks at the time of treatment initiation should receive NVP plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC, or RAL (for infants weighing ≥2 kg) plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC.

correct: For HIV, Preterm infants with a postmenstrual age ≥32 weeks to <37 weeks at the time of treatment initiation should receive NVP plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC.
wrong: For HIV, Preterm infants with a postmenstrual age ≥37 weeks to <42 weeks at the time of treatment initiation should receive NVP plus ZDV plus 3TC or FTC.
